Cement made this firm. Our first job was for a cement plant, and so were most of the ones that followed. We know a works from the quarry face to the bulk loading spout.

NCement works, Kovaya

A works, from stone to bag

A cement works takes limestone out of the ground, grinds it, burns it at about 1,450 °C into hard grey nodules called clinker, and grinds the clinker with gypsum into cement. Each stage is a different kind of machine and a different kind of work for the people who keep it running.

Follow the stone through the plant. Press any stage to see what happens there and what we are called to do.

Limestone is ripped or blasted from the face, loaded and hauled to the crusher.

What we are called for

  • Rock excavation and bench preparation with heavy breakers
  • Haul roads, built and kept
  • Tippers for stone
  • Water tankers and mine vehicles

Read on: Mining and quarrying and Rock excavation.

Boulders are broken down to stone the size of a fist. It is the most violent machine in the works.

What we are called for

  • Dynamic foundations that do not crack
  • Repairs to hoppers, chutes and structures
  • Fitters and welders for liner changes
  • Clearing of spillage

Read on: Equipment foundations and Conveyors, hoppers and tanks.

Crushed stone is dried and ground, with small corrective additions, into a fine powder called raw meal.

What we are called for

  • Mill foundations
  • Alignment, levelling and grouting
  • Duct and chute repairs
  • Crews for liner changes

Read on: Alignment and grouting.

Raw meal is stored and blended, so that the kiln receives an even feed.

What we are called for

  • Silo cleaning under confined-space control
  • Discharge gate and aeration repairs
  • Rehabilitation of silo walls

Read on: Silo cleaning and Silo rehabilitation.

A tower as tall as a thirty-storey building. Raw meal falls through a series of cyclones against the rising kiln gas, and reaches the kiln nearly red-hot.

What we are called for

  • Mechanical repairs to cyclones and ducts
  • Refractory support
  • Concrete pumped to height
  • Steelwork repairs and painting

Read on: Refractory support and Painting and corrosion protection.

A rotating steel tube sixty metres or more in length, lined with brick. At about 1,450 °C the meal fuses into clinker.

What we are called for

  • Shutdown crews in three shifts
  • Refractory support
  • Civil repairs to piers and foundations
  • Emergency call-outs, at any hour

Read on: Planned shutdowns and Emergency response.

Clinker falls on to a grate and is cooled by air within minutes. The recovered heat goes back to the kiln.

What we are called for

  • Mechanical repairs during shutdowns
  • Refractory support
  • Clearing of build-up and spillage

Read on: Maintenance and shutdowns.

Clinker waits here. Some of it leaves the works by road and by the jetty.

What we are called for

  • Silo repairs
  • Clinker haulage by tipper
  • Roads and hardstands

Read on: Bulk haulage.

Clinker is ground with gypsum, and often with fly ash or slag, into cement.

What we are called for

  • Mill foundations
  • Alignment and grouting
  • Crews for liner changes
  • Haulage of gypsum and fly ash

Read on: Equipment foundations and Bulk haulage.

Cement goes into bags or into bulk carriers, and leaves by road, rail and sea.

What we are called for

  • Vacuum-dewatered floors for packing plant and godowns
  • Roads that carry bulk carriers
  • Bulk carriers and trailers
  • Shift buses for the people who run it all

Read on: Industrial flooring and Staff and shift transport.

What a cement plant asks of a contractor

The shutdown, finished inside its window
The whole year’s production rests on a few weeks of maintenance. See Planned shutdowns.
Somebody who comes at once
A kiln that stands cold for a shift never makes those tonnes back. See Emergency response.
Foundations that do not move
Crushers and mills destroy anything less. See Equipment foundations.
Silos that stay sound
Thirty years of salt and load. See Silo rehabilitation.
Roads that carry bulkers
All day, every day, through the monsoon. See Roads and drainage.
Material that keeps moving
Limestone, coal, gypsum, clinker and cement. See Bulk haulage.
People at the gate
Three shifts, on time. See Staff and shift transport.

What cement taught us

  1. Time is production

    In heavy industry time is not money. It is production, and lost production is not recovered.

  2. Dust gets into everything

    Bearings, eyes, lungs, concrete and paint. Housekeeping is not tidiness. It is maintenance.

  3. Heat lingers

    A vessel that was shut down yesterday can still burn the hand that touches it today.

  4. Stored powder is not solid ground

    Nobody stands on it, and nobody stands under it.

  5. The plant’s rules are the rules

    Every works has its own permit system, its own gate procedure and its own way of doing things. A contractor who argues with them is not asked back.

Built here, known here

This belt is one of the great cement-producing districts of western India. Two integrated works stand within a few kilometres of our base, each with its own mines, kilns and jetty. Our supervisors have spent their working lives inside plants like these.

That is why an ATKAYVA crew does not need a week to find its way around. See Proximity.

What a port asks for

Ground that carries weight
Container stacks, reach stackers and laden trailers load a pavement more heavily than any highway.
Ground that was once sea
Much port land is reclaimed. Foundations go on piles or rafts.
Drainage
A flat yard at sea level, in a monsoon. Water has to be given somewhere to go.
Work without interruption
A yard is handed over in strips. A road is rebuilt in halves. Cargo keeps moving alongside.
Movement of project cargo
Heavy and awkward pieces, from quay to site.
People and machines at short notice
Because ships do not wait.

What we bring

Heavy-duty paving

Concrete pavements and hardstands for yards, gates and internal roads.

Industrial flooring

Warehouse and shed floors for cargo that arrives on wheels.

Piles, caps and rafts

Foundations in weak and reclaimed ground.

Stormwater works

Drains, culverts and outfalls.

Port cargo movement

Trailers and low-loaders between the quay, the yard and the plant.

Machinery and manpower

On call, from a few kilometres away.

Working inside a port

A port is a secure customs area with its own traffic, its own permits and no patience for delay.

  • Every person and vehicle is registered before entry.
  • Work areas are fenced off from cargo traffic, lit and marshalled.
  • Lifting and excavation are coordinated with terminal operations hour by hour.
  • Nothing is left where a reach stacker might find it in the dark.

The port on our doorstep

Pipavav handles containers, dry bulk, liquids and cars, and it is the first port in India connected to the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor. It has announced a large expansion across all of them. Around it stand tank terminals, container yards and warehouses, with more to come.

All of that is civil work, steel, haulage and manpower, a few kilometres from our gate. See The industrial neighbourhood.

Alexander the Great

Strategy, 356 to 323 BCE

Tyre stood on an island half a mile off the coast and had never been taken. In 332 BCE he had his army build a causeway of stone and timber out through the sea to its walls. It took seven months. Sand has gathered against that causeway ever since, and Tyre is no longer an island.

Qualified by test, in the positions the work demands.

A yard lifts all day. Blocks, plates, engines, pipes.

Shop floors, assembly areas, crane tracks and roads.
Painters and blasters
A hull is the largest coating job there is.
Flexibility
Work arrives in waves. A repair contract can need three hundred people for two months and then thirty.

What we bring

Our manpower pillar was built for exactly this pattern of demand. A core of specialists, a tested register behind it, and the ability to field people within 72 hours and stand them down when the wave has passed.

Skilled trades

Welders qualified in the 6G and 4G positions, fitters and riggers, with supervisors.

The same discipline, a different vessel

A ship under construction is a confined space made of steel, full of hot work, with people above and below each other. A cement plant in shutdown is much the same thing. Permits, gas tests, fire watches and tethered tools carry over without translation.

The yard on our doorstep

The shipyard at Pipavav has a dry dock of 662 by 65 metres, the largest in India, on a site of 600 acres. It has returned to work under new ownership and is taking on commercial and offshore vessels. A yard of that size, coming back to life, will need trades in number. Many of them already live within a bus ride of its gate.

What a mine asks for

Excavation in rock
Overburden removed, benches developed, sumps and ramps cut.
Haul roads
Built, graded and watered, so that loaded trucks can run on them safely all year.
Movement of stone
From face to crusher, and of waste to the dump.
Drainage
A pit collects every drop that falls on it.
Small civil works
Crusher foundations, retaining walls, workshops and magazines.
Vehicles

Heavy excavators and breakers

Earthmoving

Tippers

For stone and waste.

Site vehicles and water tankers

Mines have their own law

A mine is governed by its own safety legislation and its own inspectorate, and by the rules of the mine’s manager. Our operators and drivers are inducted by the mine before they enter. Vehicles carry the fittings the mine requires. We work where and how the mine’s officials direct.

We are not a mine operator and we do not blast. We provide machines, haulage, civil works and vehicles to those who are.

The stone under our feet

The miliolite limestone of this coast is the reason the cement works are here. At Babarkot the bed is 10 to 30 metres thick. We have been digging in it, and in the basalt beneath, since 2015. See The ground beneath us.

Energy: gas, wind and sun

Saurashtra has wind off the sea, eight months of clear sky, and a gas terminal on its shore. Each needs foundations in hard rock or soft ground, far from any town, built by people who do not mind the distance.

2 min read

NLNG port breakwater
On this page

  2. Sun
  3. Transmission
  4. Gas and power
  5. Where we stand
Industries

  • Ports and logistics
  • Shipbuilding

And beyond the plant wall

  • Energy
  • Tank terminals
  • Textiles and manufacturing
  • Roads and public works

Wind

A wind turbine stands on a block of concrete the size of a small house, buried in the ground. The block is a mass pour, usually in hard rock, on a hilltop reached by a road that had to be built first.

What it needs
Access roads for long, heavy loads. Excavation in rock. Dense reinforcement set round an anchor cage to fine tolerance. A continuous pour of several hundred cubic metres. Crane hardstands.
What we already do
Rock excavation. Mass concrete. Bolt placement to fine tolerance. Roads.

A turbine foundation is a machine foundation, a mass pour and a rock excavation at once, on a remote site. We have practised each of those for ten years.

Sun

A solar park is thousands of small foundations and a great deal of trenching.

What it needs
Piled or cast foundations for module mounting structures, by the thousand. Cable trenches. Internal roads and drainage. Inverter and control buildings. Boundary works.
What we already do
Repetitive foundation work at pace, trenching and drains, plant buildings, and crews that scale.

Transmission

Between a park and the grid run towers and substations.

What it needs
Tower foundations at intervals across open country. Substation civil works.
What we already do
Mobile crews and machines. Substation buildings.

Gas and power

The LNG terminal at Jafrabad, the captive power plants of the cement works and the tank farms at Pipavav are conventional heavy industry: equipment foundations, pipe racks, roads and buildings, built under strict rules for hot work and hazardous areas. See Tank terminals.

Where we stand

We will say this plainly. Cement, not energy, is where our record was made. What we offer the energy sector is a civil contractor that already works in this rock and this climate, with machines and people already here, and with the mass-concrete and foundation skills the work demands.

We are positioning ATKAYVA as a primary civil partner for the energy parks of Saurashtra. The Amreli uplands already carry wind and hybrid farms, and the waters off Pipavav have been earmarked for Gujarat’s first offshore wind farm. See The road ahead.

A teacher for this page

Nikola Tesla

Electrical engineering, 1856 to 1943

His induction motor of 1888 has no brushes and nothing that sparks. A rotating magnetic field drags the rotor round after it. Together with alternating current it meant that power could be made at Niagara and used in a factory miles away.

What we tookEvery mill drive and fan in a cement works is his motor, grown large. We set them on their foundations, and we are getting ready for the wind and sun that will feed them.

Buildings
Large clear spans, strong floors and tight envelopes.

Flat, hard and free of dust, for machines that run at high speed and trolleys that never stop.

Why a local firm

The coastal highway through this district is being widened to four lanes. The port has its own road and rail links. Villages need approach roads, drains and public buildings. Every such contract, however large its main contractor, is finally executed by machines, tippers and people from the district.

A main contractor from outside can bring its own fleet across the state. Or it can call a firm that is already here, that knows where the rock lies and which quarry gives good stone.

Ready for tenders

In 2025 the firm reorganised itself for larger contracts. How to add us as a vendor is on Becoming our client, and the documents a tender asks for can be requested through Document requests.

After a storm

When a cyclone has passed, the first need is machines: to clear roads, lift fallen structures and reopen access. A network of machines within a few kilometres is worth more in that week than a larger one two districts away.
